## Campaign Monitor Integration with Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/integrations-available-in-wp-fluent-form/campaign-monitor-integration/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/integrations-available-in-wp-fluent-form/campaign-monitor-integration/)

**Campaign Monitor**drives results with email marketing. It shares how to gain loyal customers with personalized email campaigns and automated customer journeys.

Use Fluent Forms to collect customer information and automatically add it to your Campaign Monitor list.

Integrate your **Campaign Monitor******account easily with **Fluent Forms Pro** and send emails to your subscribers without difficulty.

Let’s dive into this article to learn how to integrate**Campaign Monitor**with Fluent Forms.

### Steps to integrate Campaign Monitor with Fluent Forms

1. Activate the Campaign Monitor module
2. Get your Campaign Monitor API key & Client ID
3. Use the API key & Client ID with the Campaign Monitor Module
4. Create/Use a form with Fluent Forms
5. Setup the integrations feed and Map the input fields

- Go to the **Integration Modules** from **Fluent Forms** (WordPress admin panel sidebar) and turn on the **Campaign Monitor**Module, as shown in the screenshot below.

![Campaign Monitor Mudole Fluent Forms](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Integration-Modules-campaign_monitor.png)

- Again hover over **Fluent Forms Pro** and go to Settings. Select **Campaign Monitor,** and you will be asked for the **Campaign Monitor API Key and Client ID**here.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/camp.png)

- If you don’t have a Campaign Monitor account, you can sign up[here](https://www.campaignmonitor.com/).

- Now, Go to the **Account Settings** **→ API Keys.**

![Campaign Monitor API Fluent Forms](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Account-settings-Campaign-Monitor.png)

- Generate an API key, then Copy the API Key and Client ID to use them in the next step.

![Campaign Monitor Get API ](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Manage-API-Keys-Campaign-Monitor.png)

- Now paste them to the Campaign Monitor **Global Settings** tab in Fluent Forms & click on the **Save Settings**button.

![Campaign Monitor Paste API in settings Fluent Forms](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/adding_api_key_campaign_monitor_FluentForms.png)

- Now go to the particular form’s settings for the entries you want to be listed in **Campaign Monitor**. Click on **Add New Integration**and select **Campaign********Monitor******Integration from the dropdown.

![Campaign Monitor setup integrations Fluent Forms](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Form-Integrations-Fluent-Forms_Campaign_monitor.png)

- Name the feed and select the Campaign Monitor fields from the dropdown.

- Configure the fields and map them to the Campaign Monitor list’s corresponding rows.

![Campaign Monitor Mapping fields in Fluent forms](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/map_feed_campaign_monitor.png)

- Enable **ReSubscription**if required.

- Enable **Conditional Logic** if required. Learn more about Fluent Forms Conditional logic [here](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/conditional-logic-fluent-form/).

- Click on **Create****CampaignMonitor** **Feed** when the configuration is done.

**ActiveCampaign**is an integrated email marketing, marketing automation, and small business CRM. Save time while growing your business with sales automation.

Integrate your **ActiveCampaign**account easily with **Fluent Forms Pro** and send emails to your users with no hassle

Let’s dive into this article to learn how to integrate **ActiveCampaign**with Fluent Forms.

2. Get your ActiveCampaign API URL & API key
3. Use the API key & URL with the ActiveCampaign module

**GetResponse**is an email marketing platform. It enables you to send email newsletters, campaigns, online surveys, and follow-up autoresponders. Simple, easy interface. Use Fluent Forms to collect customer information and automatically add it to your GetResponse list.

Integrate your GetResponse account easily with **Fluent Forms Pro** by following the steps mentioned below –

### Steps to Integrate GetResponse with Fluent Forms

1. Activate the GetResponse Module
2. Get the API Key
3. Use the API key with the GetResponse module
4. Create/Use a Form with Fluent Forms
5. Setup Integrations feed & Map the GetResponse fields

- Go to the**Integration Modules** from **Fluent Forms** (WordPress admin panel sidebar) and turn on the **GetResponse**Module, as shown in the screenshot below-

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Integrations-‹-Fluent-Forms-Test-—-WordPress-12.png)

- Name the Feed & select the **GetResponse** fields from the dropdown.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Add-New-GetResponse-Integration-Feed-Fluent-Forms.png)

## User Login Requirement in Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/user-login-requirement/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/user-login-requirement/)

Enabling Fluent Forms **User Login Requirement** functionality will ensure that only your registered users can fill up a form, not others.

- First, go to **Settings & Integrations**of the form you want to Enable the login requirement.

- Then move to **Form Settings →** **Scheduling & Restrictions** (below **Form Layout**)

- In the Login Requirement Settings, Toggle on **Require user to be logged in**.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Scheduling-Restrictions-Fluent-Forms.png)

- Define the message to be shown to your unregistered / logged-out users.

- Click on **Save Settings** after your customization is done.

## Restrict Blank Form Submission with Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/restrict-blank-form-submission/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/restrict-blank-form-submission/)

Blocking users from submitting blank forms is easy. Enabling this functionality also enables you to block out spam.

- First, go to the **Settings** of the Form you want to be free from blank submissions.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Forms-FluentForm-4.png)

- Now, move into the Form **Settings & Integrations →** **Scheduling & Restrictions** (below **Form Layout**)

- Toggle on **Deny empty submission** in **Empty Submission Blocking**.

- Define the message to be shown to users when a blank form is submitted.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Scheduling-Restrictions-Fluent-Forms-1.png)

- Click on******Save Settings** when the customization is done.

## Error Message Customization with Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/error-message/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/error-message/)

Set **Error Messages** to be shown when a user fails or forgets to fill out required input fields. Error Messages can be set in [Fluent Forms](https://wordpress.org/plugins/fluentform/) to make your forms more understandable to the audience.

- First,go to the **Input** **Customization** tab of the input field you want **Error Messages** to be displayed.

- Make sure that **Yes** is selected in the **Required** option then the field will show the Error message. If **No**, the field will not be eligible to show any Error message.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Editor-Fluentform-6-1.png)

- Set the **Error Message** as required.

- Don’t forget to **Save**the Form.

- Error Messages can be positioned and presented in different ways.

- To do this, go to the **Settings & Integration →** **Form Layout** (below **Form Settings**)

- Choose your preference in the Error Message Placement option (scroll down).

- **Below Input Fields** – It will show the error message below the blank input field.

- **Stacked after Form** – Choosing **Stacked after Form**will present a list of all the required fields that were not filled up below the form.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Form-Layout-Fluent-Forms-2.png)

- Click**Save Settings**when you are done with the customization.

---

## Help Message Customization in Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/help-message/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/miscellaneous/help-message/)

**Help message** will be shown as a tooltip next to the sidebar or below the field. Help Messages can be set in [Fluent Forms](https://wordpress.org/plugins/fluentform/) to make your forms more understandable to the audience.

- First, go to the **Input** **Customization** tab of the input field for which you want **Help Messages**to be displayed.

- Then, move into **Advanced** **Options** **→ Help Message**.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Editor-Fluentform-7.png)

- Set the **Help Message** as required.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Editor-Fluentform-5-1.png)

- Don’t forget to **Save**the Form.

- Help Messages can be positioned and presented in different ways.

- To do this, go to **Settings & Integrations**→**Form Layout** (below **Form Settings**).

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Form-Layout-Fluent-Forms-1.png)

- In the Help Message Position option, you can choose your preferences.

- **Beside Label (Tooltip)** – It shows the Help Message as a Tooltip.

- **Below Input Fields**– It will show the Help message below the blank input field (not as a placeholder).

- **Focus on Element** – Choosing Focus on the Element presents the Help message only when that particular field is selected.

- **Before Input** – Choosing Before Input will position the Help message before the input field.

- Click on**Save Settings**when you are done with the customization.

## Form Scheduling Feature in Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/form-scheduling/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/form-scheduling/)

The [Fluent Forms](https://wordpress.org/plugins/fluentform/) Scheduling feature allows you to schedule a form’s live period easily. This scheduling feature enables admins to set an opening date and a closing one for particular forms, i.e., users will not be able to fill up forms before or after the schedule set by admins.

Here is how you can schedule a form with Fluent Form.

- Go to**Fluent Forms →** **All Forms**.

- Select the form you want the scheduling to be imposed on, and click the**Edit**button below it.

- Click on the**Settings & Integration**tab on the top bar and stay on the**Form Settings**section. Scroll down to the Scheduling and Restrictions segment.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Confirmation-Settings-Fluent-Forms-3.png)

- Toggle on the**Form Scheduling**feature.

- Define the weekdays from Monday to Sunday, and check all if required.

- Define the starting and ending date of that particular form.

- Define the Form Waiting message (the message to be shown before the starting date).

- Define the Form Expiration message (the message to be shown after the ending date).

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Confirmation-Settings-Fluent-Forms-2.png)

- **Save**the Form Scheduling before you leave. Otherwise, this functionality will not work.

---

## Form Restrictions Feature in Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/form-restrictions/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/form-restrictions/)

With the **Fluent Forms** Restriction feature, you can easily restrict the number of entries allowed, even on a daily/weekly/monthly/annual basis!

- Go to**Fluent Forms →** **All Forms**.

- Select the form you want the restrictions to be imposed on, and click the**Edit**button below it.

- Click on the**Settings & Integrations**tab on the top bar and stay on the**Form Settings**section. Scroll down to the Scheduling and Restrictions segment.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Confirmation-Settings-Fluent-Forms.png)

- Toggle on the**Maximum Number of Entries**feature.

- Define the maximum number of entries allowed for that particular form.

- Define the time interval from the adjacent dropdown menu. The restrictions will be effective according to the defined time interval.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Confirmation-Settings-Fluent-Forms-1.png)

- Define the message to show the users once the quota is filled up.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/max_entries_msg.png)

- **Save** the Settings. Otherwise, this restriction will not be functional.

---

## Conditional Email Notification in Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/conditional-email-notification/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/advanced-features-functionalities-in-wp-fluent-form/conditional-email-notification/)

Via email notification, [get notified every time someone fills up a form](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/how-to-use-wp-fluent-form/email-notification/). With [Fluent Forms, you can also get notified](https://wordpress.org/plugins/fluentform/) or notify your team members only when a form is filled up with a particular trigger action.

To enable this, go through the following steps –

- Click on**Edit**of the form you want email notification enabled.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/All-Forms-FluentForm-3.png)

- Go to**Settings & Integrations (topbar) → Email Notifications (sidebar)**

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-1.png)

- Click on**Add Notification**.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-2.png)

- Name the Email Notification.

- Select**Enter Email**in the**Send To**field and define the email address towhich you want your email notifications delivered. This address can be your website admin’s email address or whatever address suits you.

- Define the**Subject**of the notification email. You can also add data from submitted entries using the dropdown list of the input fields in your form for ease of use.

- Configure the Email Body the way you want to see your preferred orientation. Use the**Add Shortcodes**drop-down for ease of use. Also, for advanced customization, edit the message body in HTML codes in the**Text**tab.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-3.png)

- In the**Advanced**Email notification settings, you can configure if someone else also needs to be notified of an entry submission (your teammates, support staff, etc)

- Define the**From Name**,**Email Address**, andReply-To address that is to be shown in the notification email sent to the addressees of the notification email. And define which email addresses the notification emails will be sent to in the BCC field.

- Define the condition for which these confirmation emails will be sent.

- Select **Any**if the submissions require responding to any of the defined conditions. Select **All**if the field requires to fulfill multiple conditions.

- Define the Input fields that the conditional emails would rely upon.

- Define what logics are to be satisfied- equal/not equal, greater than/less than, contains, start with/ends with.

- Define the conditions or values that are to be met.

- You can attach any media file or document here.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-4.png)

- When all is set, click on the **Save Notification**button. Otherwise, this notification setup will not be effective.

---

The above table example was created by **Ninja Tables Pro**. You can click the boxes and notice the changes in the table. In this guide, you’ll learn how to correctly use **Custom filters** to your tables. Ninja Tables offers you a powerful feature known as Custom Filters, which lets users filter data from tables in various ways.

Go to the NinjaTables dashboard, to enable custom filters on your table. Then go to the **Edit** button of your preferred table. You can see the button when you hover your cursor on the title of the table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.1-2-1024x331.png)

Next, a Table Configurations tab will appear along with the other tabs.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.2-2.png)

Clicking the Configuration tab,  you will find a new window appear with the **Custom Filters** option on the sidebar. See in the example below:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.3-2.png)

Click on the Custom Filters, there a new tab will open with an **Add New Filter** button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.4-1-1-1024x442.png)

Click the button, then a pop-up form with a set of configuration options will open. Here’s the Pop-up Form screenshot:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.5-1-1.png)

This pop-up has a variety of options to choose from, to make your table’s filter more interactive. The following options can be found in the custom filter pop-up form:

**→ Filter Title:**This field of input is for the filter title which determines what the filter name will be.

→ **Filter Label:**This input field is used if you want to add a label to your filter. Keep it blank if you don’t need any filter instruction in the frontend.

→ **Filter UI Type:**You can choose the type of filter to display the base of the filter in the frontend. There are eight subsets in the Filter UI type. Such as- **a)** **Select Dropdown b) Radio c) Checkbox d) Date Picker e) Date Range f) Text Input g) Number Range h) Reset Filter Button**

**→ Default Label (placeholder):**To reset the table, the default placeholder is **All**. But if you want to change the text you can do it by typing in your desired text.

→ **Filter Options:**This lets you place the value through which the filter will be implemented. Put your desired values to display it on the frontend, be aware that those values need to match your cell data on that table. Filter options feature three sequential fields called **Label**, **Filter Value,** and **Action Button**:

- The label of the filtered value is entered in the Label field.
- Put the value that you want to get filtered in the Filter Value field.
- There are 2 action buttons to add and delete in each of the Label and Filter Value fields.

→ **Filter Columns:**This option is to pick the columns you wish to apply the filter. You can choose any single columns, or you can pick multiple columns.→ **Strict Mode:**Enable this mode if you want the results to be accurately matching the values.

#### Some Advance feature of Custom filter

You are going to get a few amazing features after the release of Ninja Tables 3.4.1 version. And Select Range Filter is one of them.

If you have a table like this with a column numeric column and you would like to include the option to filter by selecting the range, then you can quickly do it like this:

| Name | Age |
| --- | --- |
| Jane | 12 |
| John | 20 |
| Doe | 5 |
| Rane | 14 |
| Abrah | 7 |
| Rone | 32 |
| Simon | 21 |

Simply set the filter value to this:

- For less than **{lt} yourValue**
- For greater than **{gt} yourValue**
- Between two value **~firstValue: lastValue**

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/scrfilterselect-1024x481.png)

That is how you can use the Ninja Tables to create and add a custom filter on your table in different ways.

## Using and Customizing Pre-built Quick Forms in Fluent Forms

**Fluent Forms**comes with many pre-built **Quick Forms** to save you time. Here is how you can deploy and customize them.

## Send Users Email Notification with Fluent Forms

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/how-to-use-wp-fluent-form/send-users-email-notification-wp-fluent-form/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/fluent-form/how-to-use-wp-fluent-form/send-users-email-notification-wp-fluent-form/)

Here is another kind of email notification you can send using the Email Notification feature. If you want to send your subscriber a notification of what they have submitted to your form and confirm it, you can do that too using the Email Notification system in [Fluent Forms](https://wordpress.org/plugins/fluentform).

- Go to**Settings**of a form**→ Email Notifications**(sidebar)**→ Add Notification**& Name the notification.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-5.png)

- Choose**Select a Field**in**Send To**option.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-5-1.png)

- To configure this feature, define an Email input field in your form whose value will receive the confirmation email. You can select this field from the drop-down menu beside the**Send To Field**.

- Configure the**Subject**& **Message**that is to be sent out to the entries in the following fields. Use the**Add Shortcodes**drop-down for ease of use. Also, edit the message body in HTML codes in the Text tab for advanced customization.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-2-1.png)

- In the**Advanced**option, you can also define the From Name, Email Address, and Reply-Toaddress that is to be shown in the notification email sent to the addressees of the notification email. And define which email addresses the notification emails will be sent to in the**BCC**field.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Email-Notifications-Fluent-Forms-4-1.png)

- When all is set, click on the**Save Notification**button. Otherwise, this notification setup will not be effective.

## Widgets

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/widgets/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/widgets/)

In this section of the User Guide, we will discuss the available widgets and widget areas in the theme.

Widgets are easy to manage and can be incredibly useful to have on your site.

For the theme, we have developed custom widgets and widget areas in order to provide you with even more functionality. You also have the option of creating your own custom sidebars (custom widget areas).

Widgets add content and features to your Sidebars. In order to access the widgets page go to *Appearance > Widgets*. The Widgets area on the left-hand side is composed of 2 sections:

**Available Widgets** -all the widgets you can use in your sidebars.

![widgets](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Widgets-‹-Sand-388x1024.png)

- **Archive**– You can monthly archive of your site’s Posts.
- **Calendar**– You can use this widget area to the calendar of your site’s Posts.
- **Categories**– You can use this widget area to add a list of drop-downs categories.
- **Custom Menu**– You can use this widget area to add custom menu.
- **ScienceX Custom Recent Post** – You can use this widget area to add recent posts to your site.
- **ScienceX Custom Latest Event** – You can use this widget area to add the latest events to your site.
- **Meta**– You can use this widget area to customize login, RSS, links.
- **Pages**– You can use this widget area to customize a list of your site’s pages.
- **Recent Comments**– You can use this widget area to customize the site’s more recent comments.
- **Recent Posts**– You can use this widget area to customize the most recent posts
- **RSS**– You can use this widget area to entries from any RSS and Atom field.
- **Tag Cloud**– You can use this widget area to customize a cloud of your most used tags.
- **Text**– You can use this widget area to customize arbitrary text or HTML.

**Inactive Widgets** – drag widgets here to remove them from the sidebar but keep their settings. You can drag widgets to that section to remove them from the sidebar but keep their settings.

## Using Permalinks

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/using-permalinks/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/using-permalinks/)

Permalinks are the permanent URLs of your blog posts or pages on your WordPress site.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Permalink-Settin-1024x930.png)

1. Go to Settings > Permalinks.
2. Select one of the available formats:
- **Plain:**http://www.yourwebsite.com/?p=123
- **Day and name:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/2008/03/31/sample-post/
- **Month and name:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/2008/03/sample-post/
- **Numeric:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/archives/123
- **Post name:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/sample-post
- **Custom structure** in the box enters the custom structure you want to use. For example: /archives/%year%/%monthnum%/%day%/%postname%/
3. In the Optional section you’ll find 2 prefixes used in URLs for category and tag archives:
- **Category base** box enters the custom prefix for your category URLs.
- **Tags base** write the custom prefix for your tag URLs
4. Don’t forget to click the Save Changes button
- After, you should receive two messages regarding your .htaccess
- In case your .htaccess is writeable you will receive this message: Permalink structure updated
- In case you .htaccess is not writeable you will get this message: You should update your .htaccess

## General Settings

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/general-settings/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/general-settings/)

The General Settings page controls some of the most basic configuration settings for your site: your site’s title and location, who may register an account at your site, and how dates and times are calculated and displayed.

![settings](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/General-Settings-940x1024.png)

- **Site Title**– lets you enter the name of your site (or blog).
- **Tagline**– your site’s slogan, or short phrase, or sentence, used to convey the essence of the site and is often funny or eye-catching.
- **WordPress Address (URL)**– the full URL of the directory containing your WordPress core application files (e.g., wp-config.php, wp-admin, wp-content, and wp-includes). For example, if you installed WordPress into a directory called “blog”, then the WordPress address would be http://example.net/blog (where example.net is your domain). If you installed WordPress into your web root, this address will be the root URL http://example.net.
- **Site Address (URL)**– the address you want people to type in their browser to reach your WordPress site. This is the directory where WordPress’s main index.php file is installed. The Site address (URL) is identical to the WordPress address (URL) (above) unless you are giving WordPress its own directory.
- **E-mail Address**– the email address to which you want WordPress to send messages regarding the administration and maintenance of your WordPress site. For example, if you allow new users to register as a member of your site (see Membership below), then a notification will be sent through e-mail to this address.
- **Membership**– check this checkbox if you want anyone to be able to register an account on your site.
- **New User Default Role** – this pull-down box allows you to select the default Role that is assigned to new users.
- **Timezone** – lets you select your timezone, choose a city that is in the same timezone as you are.
- **Date Format**– the format in which to display dates on your site.
- **Time Format** – the format in which to display times on your site.
- **Week Starts On**– lets you select your preferred start date for WordPress calendars from the drop-down box, Monday being the default setting.
- **Site Language** – the WordPress dashboard language.

## Menu Creation

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/menus/menu-creation/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/menus/menu-creation/)

To create a new menu, navigate to **Appearance > Menus**from your WordPress admin panel and click on **Create a new menu**. Enter a name for your new menu and then click **Create Menu**.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/menu-1.png)

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/menu1-1.jpg)

Every page that you have created will be listed in the section on the left named **Pages**. Simply check the pages that you would like to add to your menu and click the **Add to Menu** button. Once you have added pages to your menu, you can click and drag the menu items to rearrange them or nest them one underneath the other.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/menu4-1.jpg)

In the **Menu Settings** section (which is located underneath the *Menu Structure* section), check the checkbox next to **Top menu** and click **Save Menu**. This will activate the menu you have just created, and you should now see a functional menu in your header.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/menu5-1.jpg)

You can edit your menus in the **Edit Menus**tab. When editing menus, you can click on the small triangle icon on each menu item to open a list of editable settings:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/menu9-1.jpg)

Also, you can change settings in Customize menu.

1.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/customize-1.png)

## Child and Parent Theme

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/troubleshooting-faq/child-and-parent-theme/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/troubleshooting-faq/child-and-parent-theme/)

A WordPress child theme takes the functionality of another theme, named parent theme. It gives you the possibility to customize an existing theme. Instead of modifying the theme files directly, you can activate the child theme and work within it. All customizations are stored in the child theme and anything in the child takes priority over the parent. So if the same file exists in both child and parent, the file from the child will control that aspect of the theme.

Working with child themes, your customizations are safeguarded from future upgrades because you only upgrade the parent theme, which you never edit, while the customizations are protected in your child theme which you don’t upgrade.

**Why use a Child Theme?**
**Safe Updates.** You can easily modify your website using child themes without ever changing the parent theme. When a new version of the parent theme appears, you can safely update it as all your modifications are saved in the child theme.

**Easy to Extend.** A child theme has a great flexibility. It does not require writing a lot of code. You can modify only those template files and functions that you need.

**Notice!** When you install one of our themes you must upload both parent and child theme folders to /wp-content/themes/ but you should only activate the Child theme via Appearance > Themes.

**Modifying files from the Parent theme folder**
While you should never edit files in your Parent theme, if you really must, the safest way to do it is to download a copy of the file you want to modify on your computer, make the changes, and then upload it into your child theme folder.

This way of modifying the files can be used for any files from the parent theme — note that you must re-create the same folder structure in your child theme that exists in the parent theme in order for the modifications to take effect.

## Troubleshooting FAQ

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/troubleshooting-faq/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/troubleshooting-faq/)

1. Why can’t I save my menu?
WordPress by default has a limited number of menu items. When you import our demo content, which contains a lot of menu items, you might not be able to save changes you make to a menu. You can fix this problem by contacting your hosting and asking them to add the following lines to the php.ini file:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Screen-Shot-2018-09-27-at-5.33.40-PM.png)

2. Why is there a smiley displayed on blank pages?
This problem is most likely related to JetPack and memory settings of your hosting. You can either disable JetPack or read what the JetPack developer wrote: Regarding the memory limit, please refer to the WordPress Codex section concerning this problem. Some sites that load many plugins alongside WordPress ultimately require a higher memory limit than WordPress defaults to, but since this is limited to specific hosts and configurations, it must be dealt with on an individual basis. You’ll find the Codex article at [http://codex.wordpress.org/Common_WordPress_Errors#Allowed_memory_size_exhausted](http://codex.wordpress.org/Common_WordPress_Errors#Allowed_memory_size_exhausted)

3. How do I optimize my site?
Please use this tool to investigate reasons for slow loading: [https://developers.google.com/speed/pagespeed/insights/?hl=en](https://developers.google.com/speed/pagespeed/insights/?hl=en)

4. How to translate or rename default theme labels?
You can use the Poedit software ([http://poedit.net/wordpress](http://wordpress.org/plugins/codestyling-localization/)) to translate/rename all the theme’s labels. Another solution is to edit the theme folder/languages/en_US.po file directly in a text editor and manually edit the labels you want to translate.

5. Why do I see a white screen when importing demo content?
If you get a white screen or some other error when trying to import our demo content, this probably happens because of the maximum execution time limit or max upload file size. You need to increase the maximum execution time (upload time) setting of your web server. The default maximum execution time on web servers is 30 seconds. Please increase it to 120 seconds. Also you may have to increase a limitation of Upload File Size with your Hosting Provider to Max Upload File Size. Possible ways of achieving this are:

- By Wp-config.php changes – set_time_limit(120);
- In htaccess – php_value max_execution_time 120;
- In php.ini file – max_execution_time = 120

Ask your hosting provider to take care of this for you.

## Installing Science-X

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/getting-started/installing-science-x/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/sciencex-multipurpose-education-researcher-professor-wordpress-theme/getting-started/installing-science-x/)

After downloading the **Science-X** installation file from our [official site](https://wpmanageninja.com/downloads/sciencex-multipurpose-researcher-professor-education-wordpress-theme) or [WordPress.org](https://wordpress.org/themes/sciencex-lite), then extract it and in the extracted folder locate the *sciencex.zip* file. You can then install the **Science-X** theme using one of two methods described below.

It really doesn’t matter at all which one of these techniques you want to use, so choose the one which seems to make more sense to you.

1. **WordPress upload** – For most users, this is probably the simplest installation method. To install the **Science-X** theme using this method, please follow these steps:
1. Login to your WordPress admin panel
2. Navigate to **Appearance > Themes > Add New > Upload Theme**
3. Click on **Choose File** and select *sciencex.zip*
4. Click on **Install Now**
2. **FTP upload** – If you would like to install the **Science-X** theme via FTP, please follow these steps:
1. Extract the *sciencex.zip*file you previously located. You should now see a folder named **Science-X.**
2. Using an FTP client, log-in to the server where your WordPress website is hosted
3. Using an FTP client, navigate to the */wp-content/themes/* directory under your WordPress website’s root directory
4. Using an FTP client, upload the previously extracted **Science-X****folder to the themes directory on your remote server

## Using Permalinks

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/using-permalinks/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/using-permalinks/)

Permalinks are the permanent URLs of your blog posts or pages on your WordPress site.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/permalinks.png)

1. Go to Settings > Permalinks.
2. Select one of the available formats:
- ******Plain:**http://www.yourwebsite.com/?p=123
- ******Day and name:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/2008/03/31/sample-post/
- ******Month and name:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/2008/03/sample-post/
- ******Numeric:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/archives/123
- ******Post name:** http://www.yourwebsite.com/sample-post
- ******Custom structure** in the box enters the custom structure you want to use. For example: /archives/%year%/%monthnum%/%day%/%postname%/
3. In the Optional section you’ll find 2 prefixes used in URLs for category and tag archives:
- ******Category base** box enters the custom prefix for your category URLs.
- ******Tags base** write the custom prefix for your tag URLs
4. Don’t forget to click the Save Changes button
- After, you should receive two messages regarding your .htaccess
- In case your .htaccess is writeable you will receive this message: Permalink structure updated
- In case you .htaccess is not writeable you will get this message: You should update your .htaccess

## General Settings

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/general-settings/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/general-settings/)

The General Settings page controls some of the most basic configuration settings for your site: your site’s title and location, who may register an account at your site, and how dates and times are calculated and displayed.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/general.png)

- ******Site Title**– lets you enter the name of your site (or blog).
- ******Tagline**– your site’s slogan, or short phrase, or sentence, used to convey the essence of the site and is often funny or eye-catching.
- ******WordPress Address (URL)**– the full URL of the directory containing your WordPress core application files (e.g., wp-config.php, wp-admin, wp-content, and wp-includes). For example, if you installed WordPress into a directory called “blog”, then the WordPress address would be http://example.net/blog (where example.net is your domain). If you installed WordPress into your web root, this address will be the root URL http://example.net.
- ******Site Address (URL)**– the address you want people to type in their browser to reach your WordPress site. This is the directory where WordPress’s main index.php file is installed. The Site address (URL) is identical to the WordPress address (URL) (above) unless you are giving WordPress its own directory.
- ******E-mail Address**– the email address to which you want WordPress to send messages regarding the administration and maintenance of your WordPress site. For example, if you allow new users to register as a member of your site (see Membership below), then a notification will be sent through e-mail to this address.
- ******Membership**– check this checkbox if you want anyone to be able to register an account on your site.
- ******New User Default Role** – this pull-down box allows you to select the default Role that is assigned to new users.
- ******Timezone** – lets you select your timezone, choose a city that is in the same timezone as you are.
- ******Date Format**– the format in which to display dates on your site.
- ******Time Format** – the format in which to display times on your site.
- ******Week Starts On**– lets you select your preferred start date for WordPress calendars from the drop-down box, Monday being the default setting.
- ******Site Language** – the WordPress dashboard language.

## Troubleshooting FAQ

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/troubleshooting-faq/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/troubleshooting-faq/)

### 1. Why can’t I save my menu?

WordPress by default has a limited number of menu items. When you import our demo content, which contains a lot of menu items, you might not be able to save changes you make to a menu. You can fix this problem by contacting your hosting and asking them to add the following lines to the php.ini file:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Screen-Shot-2018-09-08-at-11.18.26-AM.png)

### 2. Why is there a smiley displayed on blank pages?

This problem is most likely related to JetPack and memory settings of your hosting. You can either disable JetPack or read what the JetPack developer wrote: Regarding the memory limit, please refer to the WordPress Codex section concerning this problem. Some sites that load many plugins alongside WordPress ultimately require a higher memory limit than WordPress defaults to, but since this is limited to specific hosts and configurations, it must be dealt with on an individual basis. You’ll find the Codex article at: [http://codex.wordpress.org/Common_WordPress_Errors#Allowed_memory_size_exhausted](http://codex.wordpress.org/Common_WordPress_Errors#Allowed_memory_size_exhausted)

### 3. How do I optimize my site?

Please use this tool to investigate reasons for slow loading: [https://developers.google.com/speed/pagespeed/insights/?hl=en](https://developers.google.com/speed/pagespeed/insights/?hl=en)

### 4. How to translate or rename default theme labels?

You can use the Poedit software ([http://poedit.net/wordpress](http://wordpress.org/plugins/codestyling-localization/)) to translate/rename all the theme’s labels. Another solution is to edit the theme folder/languages/en_US.po file directly in a text editor and manually edit the labels you want to translate.

### 5. Why do I see a white screen when importing demo content?

If you get a white screen or some other error when trying to import our demo content, this probably happens because of the maximum execution time limit or max upload file size. You need to increase the maximum execution time (upload time) setting of your web server. The default maximum execution time on web servers is 30 seconds. Please increase it to 120 seconds. Also you may have to increase a limitation of Upload File Size with your Hosting Provider to Max Upload File Size. Possible ways of achieving this are:

- By Wp-config.php changes – set_time_limit(120);
- In htaccess – php_value max_execution_time 120;
- In php.ini file – max_execution_time = 120

Ask your hosting provider to take care of this for you.

## Elementor

### Why do I have an error message about Elementor?

Theme indicates the Elementor has an update, however below we can see an error message. You don’t need to pay attention to this error. We are using the Elementor Page Builder plugin as a simple layout builder with our personal widgets/elements, it should not give you any discomforts!

### Can I use Elementor Widgets/Elements?

You are able to use all the Elementor Widgets/Elements which are related to this theme (the theme is created only with that Widgets/Elements that you can use at the moment). However you can use all other Widgets/Elements, but they may not display correctly. Because they are not stylized to the theme styles.

## Child and Parent Theme

A WordPress child theme takes the functionality of another theme, named parent theme. It gives you the possibility to customize an existing theme. Instead of modifying the theme files directly, you can activate the child theme and work within it. All customizations are stored in the child theme and anything in the child takes priority over the parent. So if the same file exists in both child and parent, the file from the child will control that aspect of the theme.

Working with child themes, your customizations are safeguarded from future upgrades because you only upgrade the parent theme, which you never edit, while the customizations are protected in your child theme which you don’t upgrade.

### Why use a Child Theme?

**Safe Updates.** You can easily modify your website using child themes without ever changing the parent theme. When a new version of the parent theme appears, you can safely update it as all your modifications are saved in the child theme.

**Easy to Extend.** A child theme has a great flexibility. It does not require writing a lot of code. You can modify only those template files and functions that you need.

**Notice!** When you install one of our themes you must upload both parent and child theme folders to /wp-content/themes/ but you should only activate the Child theme via Appearance > Themes.

### Modifying Files from the Parent Theme Folder

While you should never edit files in your Parent theme, if you really must, the safest way to do it is to download a copy of the file you want to modify on your computer, make the changes, and then upload it into your child theme folder.

This way of modifying the files can be used for any files from the parent theme — note that you must re-create the same folder structure in your child theme that exists in the parent theme in order for the modifications to take effect.

## Installing Inspirar

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/getting-started/installing-inspirar/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/inspirar-pro-wordpress-theme/getting-started/installing-inspirar/)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lHwCPvqlzt8

After downloading the Inspirar installation file from WpManageNinja, extract it and in the extracted folder locate the *inspirar.zip and Inspirar-agency-child.zip* file. You can then install the Inspirar theme using one of two methods described below.

It really doesn’t matter at all which one of these techniques you want to use, so choose the one which seems to make more sense to you.

1. **WordPress upload** – For most users, this is probably the simplest installation method. To install the Inspirar theme using this method, please follow these steps:
1. Login to your WordPress admin panel.
2. Navigate to **Appearance > Themes > Add New > Upload Theme**
3. Click on **Choose File** and select *inspirar.zip*
4. Click on **Install Now.**
5. Click on **Choose File** and select I*nspirar-agency-child.zip*
6. Click on **Install Now.**
2. **FTP upload** – If you would like to install the Inspirar theme via FTP, please follow these steps:
1. Extract the *inspirar.zip*file you previously located. You should now see a folder named I*nspirar*( do the same for child theme).
2. Using an FTP client, log in to the server where your WordPress website is hosted.
3. Using an FTP client, navigate to the */wp-content/themes/* directory under your WordPress website’s root directory.
4. Using an FTP client, upload the previously extracted I*nspirar*folder to the themes directory on your remote server.

## How to create Amazon Product Comparison Table:

Here is a simple demonstration of creating an **Amazon Product Comparison table**with the help of **Ninja Tables**.

The first step is to click on the **Add Table** button. Then a pop-up window will appear that has a form to enter the required data for a table. Click the **Add**button after you are done filling up the form.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Create-a-Table-Ninja-Table.png)

Next, a table will be made where an **Add Column**button will appear to create new columns.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Add-Column-Ninja-Table.png)

Then start creating columns in the pop-up window, where a form appears with its fields.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Column-Basic-Settings-Ninja-Table.png)

A table is made with the created single column. The outcome looks like this:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Speaker-Name-Column-Ninja-Table.png)

Following the same method, make four more columns just by clicking the Add Column button on the top right corner.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Add-More-Columns-Ninja-Table.png)

Now you need to add appropriate data to the relevant column. There are no data in the field. So, click on **Add data** in the section called **Table Row**.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Add-Data-to-Column-Ninja-Table.png)

A pop-up window for entering data to the specific column will appear with a given form. Fill in the form and provide the appropriate information and press the “Add” button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Add-Data-to-All-Columns-Ninja-Table.png)

The image can also be added if you wish to

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Add-Image-to-Column-Ninja-Table.png)

Now have a text editorial look at the image given above.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Column-Data-in-text-Tab-Ninja-Table.png)

You can see in the above image a link has been set behind the image. The view of the text editor displays the link. After all the information has been entered, click on the Add button to add all the data.

Data has been included in the relevant table column. Click on the “Add Media” button to attach an image. By visual / text editor, you can also link to a text through which you can make affiliation with your desired affiliate program.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Output-of-Table-in-Preview-Mode-Ninja-Table.png)

The above image shows the output of the table in preview mode.

That is how you can bring basic data to the table. Within this image, we see that a text link has been displayed at first, and finally an image link. You can place the required data into the table in this way.

You can then add more columns and data as required. You may also delete the border if you want, and even that with a few clicks. To do this, go to “Table Design” at the top of the page and then select the “Styling” option from the right panel and finally check the “Hide all border” option at the bottom of the “Features” section.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Table-Design-Styling-Ninja-Table-1-1024x622.png)

The preview of the border-less table is given below:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Preview-After-Hide-Border-Ninja-Table-1024x145.png)

Complete the table as stated out above

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Full-Table-Setup-Ninja-Table-1-1024x507.png)

Now you can get your table configured as you like. You can change the color scheme and you can also customize color in the section “Table Color” as you want. 13 Basic colors are provided by default. Violet was selected from the drop-down list. If that doesn’t satisfy you can use the custom color.

To customize, go to the first section of Table Color located in the Table Design panel on the right. Then on the right side of the section, click on the option “Custom Scheme.” Then a four-color box appears to modify any component of the table. Those are the plugin’s additional features.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Set-Color-Ninja-Table-1024x547.png)

Given below is the final outcome of the table in the preview:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Amazon-Product-Comparison-Final-Output-Ninja-Table-1024x498.png)

## How to create a Product Specification Table:

A **Product Specification Table**is basically a demonstration which shows detailed information regarding any product. Along with the manufacturer’s credentials, it also contains details of the design, product illustrations & notes describing the products.

This tutorial will demonstrate how to make a Product Specification table using Ninja Tables. In this case, an android smartphone’s specification is created as an example.

Firstly click on **NinjaTables Pro**which will take you to the plugin’s dashboard. Then click over the **Add Table**button to create a new table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.2-1-1-1024x361.png)

Here you will notice a pop-up window with forms to add the table title and description.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Create-a-Table-Ninja-Table.png)

Click on the **Add**button to make a table after entering the required data. Next, an **Add Column**button will appear under the **Table Rows**tab. Click here to add new columns for your table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Add-Column-from-Table-Rows-Ninja-Table.png)

Or you can go to the **Table Configurations**tab. Here the column title can be added & then a new column is created by clicking the **Add Column** button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Column-Basic-Settings-from-Table-Configuration-Ninja-Table-1024x649.png)Product Specification Table

After clicking the Add Column button, a pop-up box will appear where there is a form to enter the required column details. In the same way, click on the Add Column button once all the column data has been added.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Column-Basic-Settings-from-Table-Rows-Ninja-Table.png)

Similarly, you have to make another column called Specification but you need to assign the data type as HTML field this time.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-1.7-7.png)

Next, navigate to the Table Rows tab by clicking the Add Data button to enter the data in the column in a row by row format.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Add-Data-from-Table-Rows-Tab-Ninja-Table.png)

You’ll then have a pop-up window that allows you to add data that you want to place to the table. Lastly, to include data to the list click on the Add button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Add-Data-to-All-Columns-Ninja-Table.png)

You can insert an image by clicking the Add Media button in the input field as well.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Add-Image-in-Table-Ninja-Table-824x1024.png)

You can similarly place the data one by one in the table. The final result will be as the image below after placing the required details.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Product-Specification-Table-Final-Output-Ninja-Table-458x1024.png)

This specification table is completely responsive. The table is displayed suitably in the mobile view as the plugin is designed to be mobile-friendly.

So, using the Ninja Tables WordPress plugin, you can make a completely responsive mobile friendly specification table for any sort of product. This post, hopefully, helped you find the right option.

## Creating Pricing Table for Divi Theme

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/creating-pricing-table-for-divi-theme/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/creating-pricing-table-for-divi-theme/)

**Divi** is powered by the **Divi** Builder, an amazingly accomplished WordPress Theme with a Drag & Drop Page Builder that makes it easier than ever to build beautiful WordPress websites. Before I get to how to create a pricing table for Divi theme, let me make you understand about the pricing table.

The**Pricing table** plays an important role in every organization that offers different products or services. This is a significant challenge from both a design and usability standpoint. They must be simple and easy but at the same time clearly able to differentiate between the features and prices of different products and services. Today, I am going to demonstrate the total procedures for creating a responsive pricing table for Divi theme.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-5.09.11-PM.png)

Creating a pricing table for Divi theme is as simple as other pricing table creation. In this case, I am using a beautiful WordPress plugin named[Pricing Table Builder](https://wordpress.org/plugins/wp-pricing/)plugin. First of all, you have to [download and install](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/download-install-and-activate-the-pricing-table-builder/) the plugin on your site. Then make it active and open the plugin by clicking on the plugin title located in the left sidebar of the dashboard.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-1.55.04-PM-1.png)

Then you will have a dashboard of the plugin and click on the **Add Table** button to create a new pricing table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-1.59.23-PM.png)

Then a popup window will appear to you to give the table name. Give the table title which one you want to create. Then click on **Add New** button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-2.03.05-PM.png)

A default pricing table has created after clicking the **Add New** button. Here is the look of default view of the pricing table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-11.31.58-AM.png)

Now, you can edit, add and erase the necessary parts of the table. First of all, you can change the layout from the **STYLE** section. Click on the **STYLE** and you will have two layouts and four different skins design for your table. Choose the second layout and first skin design from the STYLE section. Keep the border and the column rounded enabled for a different look.

Then go to the **CONTENT** section to make a change in the contents of the default content slider. There are three default content sliders in the plugin dashboard. Make a proper customization clicking on the particular content slider from the content section.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-11.32.16-AM.png)

You also apply drag and drop for rearranging the content column. If you want to add something, you can do this easily by clicking on the plus(+) icon located on the bottom.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-2.41.36-PM.png)

To make a change click on the specific content item, then a custom slider will open with its options.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-2.47.20-PM.png)

There are several options there for a specific customization. For the title, you can click on the **Title** option, for the features you can click on the **Features** option. Same things happen for the rest of the options.

If you click on Title, it will take you to another custom slider where y0u can edit the content.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-2.52.53-PM.png)

This is how you can change every content slider as your will. For every content slider, this is the same way to customize.

Now come to the **FEATURES**, this is as simple as the previous one. Click on the FEATURES, you will see a custom slider will open with the existing features.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.03.56-PM.png)

Now, you can change by clicking on each feature. Here, you also can rearrange the features by drag & drop facility.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.06.24-PM.png)

You can change the icon from the**ICON CLASS** as it has the default six icons.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.09.30-PM.png)

You also can add a hint text for making things easy by typing text in the input field named **HINT TEXT.**

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.26.09-PM.png)

Have a look at the preview of the configuration.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.24.43-PM.png)

These all are the features of the **CONTENTS** section.

Next, come to the **ELEMENTS** section. To make a change elements of the contents, you can go through the section. There are four different options within the section. Each section contains the same procedures.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.32.43-PM.png)

I am showing one of the options. Click on the  Title and you will be taken to a custom slider where you can customize the elements of the content.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-3.40.36-PM.png)

You can hide the title, you can change header color and font size. At the same time, you can customize the sub-title by changing the color and font size of the sub-title.

Next, click on Features option then, in the same way, you will have a custom popup for hiding features, color changing, for font size changing. Then you can have change icon color and icon font size.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-4.20.01-PM.png)

Next, click on the **Price** option, in the same way, you will have a custom popup for hiding price, change prefix color and font size. The price color and price font size can customize here. You can change postfix color and postfix font size as well.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-5.05.37-PM.png)

Now, click on the Footer option to customize it. Here in the footer part, you can hide footer, button color, button font size. You can also customize button background color, button border color, button text color and button font size.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-4.58.25-PM.png)

Now, have a look for an ultimate view of the output. This is the final viewpoint of the Divi pricing table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-18-at-5.12.55-PM.png)

That’s all for creating a pricing table of Divi theme. You can create such a wonderful pricing table for the Divi theme. Hopefully, this article helped you to make you understand creating a pricing table for any kind of purpose. If you learn more about the issue, please click on the [link.](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/creating-pricing-table)

To download the Pricing Table Builder [click here](https://wordpress.org/plugins/wp-pricing/). To learn more about Divi Theme, just [click here](https://www.softwarefindr.com/reviews/divi-theme).

## How to create Cryptocurrency Table Using Ninja Tables:

Read this simple guide to learn how to make a **Cryptocurrency table** using Ninja Tables:

### Step 1:

The first step is to click on the **Add Table**button. This will, in turn, display a pop-up window to enter the required data to make a table. Then click on the **Add**button after filling up the form. A table will be created with its column options.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-Create-Table-Ninja-Table.png)

### Step 2:

After the table is created, you will find an **Add Column**button to make new columns for the tables.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-Add-Column-Interface-Ninja-Table.png)

Click this button in order to enter the column data in the pop-up window.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-Column-Basic-Settings-Ninja-Table.png)

The table has been created with its column, that looks like this:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-Table-with-Single-Column-Ninja-Table.png)

### Step 3:

In the same way, four more columns have to be created. By clicking the **Add Column**button in that table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-5-6.png)

### Step 4:

Then you have to add relevant data to the specific column. So, go to the **Table Row** segment and click on the **Add Data**button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-6-5.png)

### Step 5:

A pop-up window to input data to the relevant column will appear with a specific form. Fill in the form providing the appropriate info and press the “Add” button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-Add-Data-to-All-Columns-Ninja-Table.png)

Data has been added to the appropriate table section. By clicking the “Add Media” button, you can add an image. You may also use a visual / text editor to link to a text.

Four data columns are added to the table in this tutorial, including text and image. The first is the currency name for preview, the second is an image with a link as a currency name that will take you directly to the respective page. The third is a price input and the fourth is simply a text with the name “24h % Change” displaying the currency’s changing state over 24 hours. You can add any additional items as you want. You can add an image button, or write code to directly add a button to it. Here is the full input view of the text editor.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-8-5.png)

And finally, here is the overview of the interface above as it would look like

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-An-Overview-Before-Final-Output-Ninja-Table-621x1024.png)

You can adjust the color by the default color scheme and the “Table Color Scheme” segment can also customize the color as you like. You have to select the “Custom” option to customize it. Then two color boxes appear for the background and text color respectively, with the name primary color and secondary color.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Figure-10-3.png)

The user can change the table color the way they want it. Such as the example below, the table color in the preview can be changed:

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cryptocurrency-Table-Final-Output-Ninja-Table-700x1024.png)

## ELEMENTS

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/configuring-with-the-section/elements/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/configuring-with-the-section/elements/)

The **ELEMENTS**section which allows you to customize/configure every element of the content slider. In this section, there are four options to configure. Each option plays a different kind of rules for a particular content slider.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-10.15.00-AM.png)

The first option of **ELEMENTS** section is **Title.** To get to that click on the option on top.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-10.24.27-AM.png)

There are five parts of the option. In the first part, you have an option of hiding the title which is **HIDE TITLE**. You can enable or disable the title using this option.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-11.19.11-AM.png)

## CONTENTS

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/configuring-with-the-section/contents/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/configuring-with-the-section/contents/)

**CONTENTS** section is used to customize all the contents available in the pricing table. There are 3 built-in content slides in the plugin. You can add as you need. Each content slide settings and configuration works in the same way. I am showing the all the system and configuration in general. In this section, you can add, edit, delete the contents altogether. To make sure I am showing you all of its functionalities. First of all, click on the **CONTENTS**section and you will be have the following options given below in the snapshot.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-4.22.52-PM.png)

You can edit existing content by clicking the content part. You also can copy by clicking on the copy icon of the respective content part. By applying the same way you can delete by clicking the delete icon. At the bottom, there is an **ADD**button to add any content needs to be added. Most importantly you can rearrange the existing contents through drag and drop.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-7.38.36-PM.png)

Let’s move to the edit part of the section by clicking the first content part itself. ![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-4.37.38-PM.png)

Then you will find a custom slider option appear to you bearing the existing contents.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-4.35.06-PM-1.png)

In this part, at first, you have an icon for featuring the existing content. If you want to do so, just enable the icon then the existing content would be the featured content.

Then come to the next, in this part, in this part you can customize the texts of the content. Click on the **Title** field to change the text of the title. I am typing **Standard** in place of **Personal Plan.**In the same way, you can change the caption part situated just under the title. I keep it the same as before.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-4.58.09-PM.png)

Then come to the body part by clicking the **Features** option.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-5.02.15-PM.png)

In this part, you will have a custom slider bearing the existing content.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-5.04.36-PM.png)

This part is almost the same as the previous one. Here just one option is given for adding for more features. To add more features just click on the **Add** icon.

You also can edit specific data by clicking on that particular data.![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-5.11.25-PM.png)

Then you will have another slider for that particular text. You can edit, add, delete and also make a text hint for this particular text.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-5.31.40-PM.png)

You can make a hint of any of the features for securing the thing user-friendly.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-2.39.41-PM-1.png)

The output is given below for your better understanding.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-2.44.52-PM.png)

You can change the feature icon from the dropdown list. There are six inbuilt icons given for the text. You can choose one of them.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-5.34.48-PM.png)

The output of the feature icon would be like so.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-2.49.07-PM.png)

This is the last option of the **Feature** part. Next, come to the **Price** part of the section. Click on the **Price** option to make any customization.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-6.45.53-PM.png)

Then you will have another custom slider for customizing pricing materials. There are 4 options for that part.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-6.45.30-PM.png)

There is a **PRICE PREFIX** option on top of the list. This option contains a drop-down bearing 3 default semi options to limit the business policy. You can choose one of them.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-7.21.29-PM.png)

Then you have **CURRENCY**option that contains 2 default currency. The good part of this is, you can add any sign of a currency as your choice.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-7.22.36-PM.png)

Then you have the input field for giving the **PRICE**. This part is used to input the price you want to add. You can use the expected number digit you want.

The last part of the PRICE option is **PRICE POSTFIX**with a drop-down option for adjusting duration of your pricing policy. This field determines how long you want to last the price offering.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-14-at-7.28.34-PM.png)

This is how the pricing option works.

Let’s get into the **Button** option. To get into the **Button** option, click on the **Button** option of the content part.  In this option, you will have five functionalities.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-9.19.27-AM.png)

First of all, there is a **BUTTON LABEL**which determines the text of the button. You can give any text you want as I have given here **Purchase**.

Next turn to the **BUTTON URL** which determines button link you want to provide. Usually, this link is directed to the purchase page where all the purchases functionalities happen.

Next, come to the **OPEN LINK IN NEW WINDOW**option that actually enables you to open a new window with the given link. It actually works as **target=”_blank”** in the programming. You can enable or disable the option using this part.

The **CAPTION** is the next part of the **BUTTON** option. This part determines the additional texts that usually say about the offerings. Typically it says about the offer duration.

The last part of the button option is **CUSTOM CLASS** which actually allows you to add any additional custom CSS into the button option. This is how the button option works.

The last part of the Content section is **MAIN SKIN COLOR** which determines the color code of the respective content slider.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-10.04.22-AM.png)

You can choose your custom color according to your choice. Here is a default custom color pad is given to customize the expected color.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-10.04.51-AM.png)

This is how y0u can use the color code of a specific part of a content slider. These are the functionalities of the **CONTENTS** section.

## Starting with Pricing Table Builder

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/creating-a-table/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/creating-a-table/)

**Pricing Table Builder** is an awesome WordPress plugin which is used to create various types of pricing table for any kind of organization. This plugin is free to download but you can buy the plugin as it has the premium version as well for having more functionalities. I think you are entirely new to this plugin and just have installed the plugin into your site then you will get the following immediate options.

If you don’t have any existing plugin then the interface would be like so.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-5.04.17-PM.png)

In this case, you just click on **Create Your First Pricing Table (in the middle of the board)** button or **Add Table(in the top right corner of the board)** button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/p3-1.png)

Or if you have existing tables on the board then the interface would be like so. In this case, you just click on the **Add Table(top right corner of the board)** button to create a new table.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/p4.png)

So far you have come to know how to integrate **Pricing Table Builder** plugin with your WordPress site. Now it’s time to create a beautiful pricing table.

To create a new pricing table click **Add Table**button, then you will have a pop-up to assign your table name. Put your expected table name in the input field and click on the **Add New** button.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/p5.png)

A new pricing table has already created according to your given name. Then you will be confirmed by a popup notification and will be directed to a new page where a default design pattern of a pricing table has given to you. Now you can customize the existing design as you need.

![](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/p6.png)

That’s how you can create a default pricing table structure after opening the plugin. Now you just need to customize according to your plan.

## Download, Install and Activate the Pricing Table Builder

**Source:** [https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/download-install-and-activate-the-pricing-table-builder/](https://wpmanageninja.com/docs/pricing-table-builder/download-install-and-activate-the-pricing-table-builder/)

#### Requirements

To use after downloading and installing Pricing Table Builder, you need:

– WordPress 4.5 or later

– PHP version 5.4 or later

#### Installing and Activating NinjaTables

Installing Pricing Table Builder is similar to any other WordPress plugins. Here are the steps:

- Navigate to – WordPress Admin Dashboard → Plugins → Add New
- Now, you can search for Pricing Table Builder, click install and activate

Alternatively, you can download the .zip file and upload it from Add New plugin page. Then click install and activate

![How to install Pricing Table Builder](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/p1-1.png)Install Pricing Table Builder
Next, after installing then activate the plugin and you will find the plugin left sidebar in your dashboard.

![How to Install Pricing Table Builder](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Screen-Shot-2018-07-16-at-4.31.07-PM.png)Install Pricing Table Builder
Then click on the plugin **Pricing Table** from your left sidebar to start using.

![How to Install Pricing Table Builder](https://wpmanageninja.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/p2.png)Install Pricing Table Builder
This is how you can download and install the Pricing Table Builder.
